subject: general
question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1931**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on **5 March 1931** between Mahatma Gandhi and the then Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin.
 
• This pact marked the end of the **civil disobedience movement** led by the Indian National Congress against British rule in India.
 
• Under the terms of the pact, the British Government agreed to **release all political prisoners** who had been detained during the civil disobedience movement.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, representing the Indian National Congress, agreed to **discontinue the civil disobedience movement** and participate in the **Second Round Table Conference** in London.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**

 
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a political agreement signed by Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin, in 1931.
 
• It was a significant event in the Indian freedom struggle, which led to the cessation of the civil disobedience movement that was initiated against the British Salt Tax.
 
• The pact included several concessions by the British Government, such as the withdrawal of all ordinances and prosecutions, release of prisoners arrested for participating in the salt march, and the return of confiscated properties of the satyagrahis.
 
• Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, the Civil Disobedience Movement aimed at disobeying certain laws, demands, and commands of the British government, particularly the Salt Act.
 
• The movement began with the Dandi March, where Gandhi and his followers marched to the Arabian Sea coast to produce salt from seawater in defiance of British laws.
 
• This movement attracted widespread participation from various sections of Indian society and was a crucial step towards India's independence.
 
• The movement saw significant government repression, including the arrest of thousands of protesters and leaders.
 
 
 
• **Second Round Table Conference**
 
 
• The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in September 1931 and was attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The conference aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India and the future governance of the country.
 
• Despite the discussions, the conference did not result in any significant agreements, leading to Gandhi's return to India and the resumption of the civil disobedience movement.
 
• The failure of the conference highlighted the deep divisions between the British authorities and Indian leaders regarding India's political future.
